ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2022-01-15
Provider: Dr. Emily Rodriguez, MD
Department: Pediatric Neurology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Abnormal posture and difficulty standing upright

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns for follow-up, having presented in January 2020 with difficulty keeping up with other children and trouble climbing stairs, and in July 2020 with progressive difficulty walking and frequent falls. The patient is brought to the clinic by his parents due to abnormal posture and difficulty standing upright, which has progressively worsened over the past several months. His parents have noticed that he walks with a waddling gait, frequently falls, and often arches his back while trying to stand. He does not complain of pain, and there is no recent trauma. He was late to begin walking but otherwise met early developmental milestones.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Duchenne muscular dystrophy (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- progressive proximal muscle weakness
- gait abnormality

ALLERGIES:
No known allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal uncle with muscular dystrophy (wheelchair-bound)
- Mother is an asymptomatic carrier of muscular dystrophy

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Kindergarten student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical examination reveals lumbar lordosis, proximal lower limb weakness, and calf muscle enlargement.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory studies show elevated serum creatine kinase.

OTHER STUDIES:
Genetic testing is pending.

attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-07-15
Provider: Dr. Michael Okonkwo, MD
Department: Medical Genetics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Progressive difficulty walking and frequent falls over the past 2 years

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns for follow-up evaluation six months after his initial presentation to Pediatrics with progressive gait abnormalities and proximal muscle weakness. His parents report that he was able to walk independently by 16 months of age but has always been slower than his peers in sports and running. Over the last year, they have noticed that he climbs stairs using both hands and pushes on his thighs to stand from a seated position. He now complains of occasional leg pain after activity and has trouble lifting his backpack.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Duchenne muscular dystrophy (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- progressive proximal muscle weakness
- gait abnormality

MEDICATIONS:
He takes no medications.

ALLERGIES:
No known allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
The patient's maternal uncle became wheelchair-bound in adolescence and died in his 20s from respiratory complications.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Kindergarten student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the boy has bilateral calf enlargement, lumbar lordosis, and a waddling gait. Strength testing shows marked weakness in the hip flexors and extensors, with relative preservation of distal limb strength. Deep tendon reflexes are diminished in the lower extremities.

LABORATORY DATA:
Serum creatine kinase is markedly elevated.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
The defective protein in this patient normally links the cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Pediatrics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Difficulty keeping up with other children and trouble climbing stairs

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
She reports that over the past year, he has had trouble climbing stairs and getting up from the floor. She often notices that he uses his hands to push on his thighs to stand upright. He has also begun to walk with a waddling gait and occasionally falls when running.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- progressive proximal muscle weakness
- gait abnormality

His prenatal and birth history were unremarkable, and developmental milestones were initially achieved on time.

ALLERGIES:
No known allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
There is no family history of neuromuscular disease.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Kindergarten student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, the child walks with a wide-based gait, has mild lumbar lordosis, and shows enlargement of the calves bilaterally. Neurologic exam reveals 4/5 strength in proximal lower extremities with intact reflexes and sensation.

LABORATORY DATA:
Serum creatine kinase level is markedly elevated.

PLAN:
Genetic testing is ordered.
